text:
I hate qualifying arguments like this, but - everyone knows I am about as pro-Ukraine/anti-Russian as it gets.  That regularly leads to friction between me and other Republicans, even ones who otherwise align 99%.

With that said, whining from Europeans and the American left about America buying $1B in diesel fuel from Russia is so out of touch with reality.  The EU has spent over $200B on Russian fuel and is on-track to buy hundreds of billions more.  Most of that was purchased by wealthy EU members who can absolutely afford alternatives.

"We're going to continue to fuel the growth of company, and that's going to be both through organic investments and inorganic investments. And we're committed to returning greater than 50% of our free cash flow on average over time, and that's all while maintaining a strong and flexible balance sheet."

name: Lisa Abramowicz
zh_summary: @lisaabramowicz1: solid credit has comforted equity traders, but that is eroding as corporate bond yields rise, especially for weak firms; yields on the lowest rated bonds are the highest since 2022.
en_summary: @lisaabramowicz1: solid credit has comforted equity traders, but that is eroding as corporate bond yields rise, especially for weak firms; yields on the lowest rated bonds are the highest since 2022.
text: A big source of comfort for equity traders has been the solid credit market. But that's been eroding in the past few weeks as corporate bond yields creep higher, particularly among weak companies. Yields on the lowest-rated bonds are now the highest since 2022.

name: Meb Faber
zh_summary: @MebFaber podcast: by Citi's math we have been in a bubble since mid last year, and Dirk Willer says keep buying; topics include why 1929 is the only bubble that crashed immediately, why the bond selloff is about growth not deficits, and gold peaking when the PBOC stops buying.
en_summary: @MebFaber podcast: by Citi's math we have been in a bubble since mid last year, and Dirk Willer says keep buying; topics include why 1929 is the only bubble that crashed immediately, why the bond selloff is about growth not deficits, and gold peaking when the PBOC stops buying.
text:
By @Citi's math, we’ve been in a bubble since mid last year, and Dirk Willer, Head of Global Macro Asset Allocation, says to keep buying.

We also cover:

• Why 1929 is the only bubble that crashed immediately
• The Warsh shadow rate and why it tracked Greenspan’s Fed
• Why the bond selloff is about growth and not deficits
• Why Brazil’s 9% to 10% real rates set up a big opportunity
• Why gold peaks when the PBOC is done buying
• His favorite bubble hedge
